---
title: "w05_Task1"
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
df <- read_csv("https://github.com/fivethirtyeight/guns-data/raw/master/interactive_data.csv")
```

```{r}
nona <- df %>% 
          filter(df$Deaths!=0& df$Population!=0 & df$Rate!=0.0 & df$Race!="None selected" & df$Gender!="None selected" & df$Age!="None selected")
View(nona)
```

```{r}
nona$Age <- factor(
  nona$Age,
  levels = c("Under 15", "15 - 34", "35 - 64", "65+")
)
```

```{r}
ggplot(nona, mapping = aes(x = Age))+
  geom_bar() +
  geom_text(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = "Top Left", hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.2)+
  geom_text(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = "Top Right", hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.2)+
  geom_text(x = -Inf, y = -Inf, label = "Bottom Left", hjust = -0.1, vjust = -0.3)+
  geom_text(x = Inf, y = -Inf, label = "Bottom Left", hjust = 1.1, vjust = -0.3)
```


Here in this visualization we can see the different age demographics that are dying from gun related incidents. 
The biggest issue that we see is that a larger percentage of young adults have died as a result of individual shootings.
While the numbers are not that far apart for any of the 4 categories we can see how we can start to affect the problem in a big way by educating younger people on the importance of gun safety.


```{r}
highrate <- nona %>%
              filter(nona$Rate>10)
View(highrate)
```
```{r}
ggplot(highrate, mapping = aes(x = Race, y = Rate))+
  geom_dotplot(binaxis = 'y')
```


This graph shows us the demographics with the highest risk of gun violence based off of population per 100000 people and death count.
It shows us that Black Americans have the highest average rate of risk of gun violence while White Americans have larger counts of high rates of gun violence.


```{r}
cleanintent <- nona %>%
              filter(nona$Intent!='None selected' & nona$Intent!='Unknown')
View(cleanintent)
```
```{r}
ggplot(cleanintent, mapping = aes(x = Age, y = Rate, fill = Intent))+
  geom_col(position = "dodge")+ 
  annotate("text", x = 2, y = 5, label = "This is a label", size = 4)
```



We can clearly see that younger grown people between the ages of 15–34 face much higher killing rates, while self-killing with guns becomes far more common among older people, most of all those aged 65 and up. The biggest warning is that younger adults face a greater threat from killings, while older adults face a stronger threat from suicide.
